capabilities.name: Quantity as a Set Property
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands that a collection has a quantity that is preserved across irrelevant changes in spacing, arrangement, or object appearance.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover the counting procedure itself, written numerals, or numerical ordering.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If you spread the same few objects farther apart without adding or removing any, does your child usually understand that there are still the same number?

capabilities.name: Counting & Cardinality
capabilities.formal_definition: Uses the counting system to determine or construct an exact quantity and understands that the final count word represents the total.
owned_skill_families: producing a requested number of objects
counting from a given starting number
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not primarily cover written numeral recognition, magnitude comparison, or arithmetic transformation.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: After counting a group of toys, if you ask “How many are there?”, does your child usually tell you the total without starting the count again?

capabilities.name: Numeral–Quantity Mapping
capabilities.formal_definition: Connects spoken and written number symbols with the exact quantities they denote.
owned_skill_families: matching equivalent symbolic and non-symbolic quantities
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover relative magnitude/order or the mechanics of counting a collection.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If you show a written number such as 7, can your child usually make or choose a group with exactly that many objects?

capabilities.name: Magnitude, Order & Number-Line Relations
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands relative numerical size, sequence position, and spatial/order relationships among numbers.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover numeral identification alone or composing numbers into parts.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Can your child usually tell which of two familiar numbers is larger even when the difference is small, such as 8 and 9?

capabilities.name: Number Composition & Part–Whole Structure
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands a number as a whole that can be composed from and decomposed into parts in multiple equivalent ways.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover solving additive situations as the main goal; it is about the internal structure of a number.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If you ask for different ways to make 8 using two groups, can your child usually find more than one combination?

capabilities.name: Additive Situation Structure
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands the semantic structures represented by joining, separating, changing, comparing, and part–part–whole additive situations.
owned_skill_families: connecting story structure to addition or subtraction
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover general cross-domain modeling or calculation strategy efficiency.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: When you describe a simple story where some objects are added, taken away, or compared, can your child usually tell what quantity needs to be found?

capabilities.name: Additive Relations & Calculation
capabilities.formal_definition: Determines sums and differences and reasons about additive relationships using increasingly structured and efficient strategies.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover place-value structure or merely identifying whether a story is additive.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If your child does not immediately know an addition answer, can they often work it out using a useful strategy instead of recounting everything from 1?

capabilities.name: Base-Ten Unitization & Place Value
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands that ten lower-order units can be treated as one higher-order unit and that digit position represents units of different sizes.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover multi-digit addition/subtraction procedures themselves.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If you show 34 as 3 groups of ten and 4 single objects, does your child understand that both representations mean the same number?

capabilities.name: Multi-Digit Additive Reasoning
capabilities.formal_definition: Uses base-ten structure to reason about and calculate multi-digit addition and subtraction.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover the underlying place-value concept in isolation.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: When adding numbers such as 27 + 15, does your child use tens and ones or another structured method rather than counting one by one?

capabilities.name: Equal Groups, Arrays & Multiplication
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands multiplication as coordinated equal groups, arrays, and composite units rather than only repeated counting.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover fair sharing/grouping division or multiplicative comparison such as “three times as many.”
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If there are 4 bags with 3 objects in each, can your child reason about 4 groups of 3 without counting all 12 objects individually?

capabilities.name: Division, Sharing & Grouping
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands division as equal sharing or determining how many equal groups can be formed.
owned_skill_families: finding unknown group size or group count
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover multiplication as the primary structure or scaling comparisons.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If 12 objects must be shared equally among 3 people, can your child usually reason out how many each person receives?

capabilities.name: Multiplicative Comparison & Scaling
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands multiplicative relationships in which one quantity is a scale factor or multiple of another.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover equal-group multiplication when no comparison or scaling relation is involved.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If one tower is 4 blocks tall and another is twice as tall, does your child understand the second tower should be 8 blocks rather than 6?

capabilities.name: Equal Partition & Unit Fraction
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands that a defined whole can be partitioned into equal shares and that one equal share represents a unit fraction.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not primarily cover comparing fraction magnitudes or equivalence among different fractions.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: When sharing one item among several people, does your child understand that the shares must be equal for them to be fair fractional parts?

capabilities.name: Fraction as Number & Magnitude
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands fractions as numbers with magnitude that can be located, ordered, and compared.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover equal partitioning as the main construct or equivalence transformations.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Can your child usually tell which of two simple fractions is larger by thinking about their size rather than only looking at the numerals?

capabilities.name: Fraction Equivalence & Composition
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands that different fractional expressions can denote the same quantity and that fractions can be composed or decomposed.
owned_skill_families: recognizing multiple representations of the same fraction
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover basic unit-fraction partitioning or decimal notation.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Does your child understand that two fourths can represent the same amount as one half when they refer to the same whole?

capabilities.name: Decimal Place Value & Magnitude
capabilities.formal_definition: Extends base-ten place-value reasoning to quantities less than one and connects decimal notation to magnitude.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover whole-number place value or fraction equivalence as the main construct.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Can your child explain why 0.7 is larger than 0.65 without treating 65 as automatically larger than 7?

capabilities.name: Repeating Pattern Structure
capabilities.formal_definition: Recognizes and reasons about a repeating unit that generates a repeating pattern.
owned_skill_families: translating a pattern to another modality
creating a pattern from a unit
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover patterns whose values systematically grow or general cross-domain structural noticing.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If a pattern is red-blue-blue, red-blue-blue, can your child identify the smallest part that keeps repeating?

capabilities.name: Growing Pattern & Functional Change
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands systematic change across successive cases and uses the growth relationship to extend or predict.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover fixed repeating units or formal equality/unknowns.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If a block pattern grows by 2 each step, can your child use that rule to predict what comes later rather than drawing every earlier step?

capabilities.name: Equality & Equivalence
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands equality as a relation stating that two quantities or expressions have the same value.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover unknown-symbol manipulation as the main construct or general argument evaluation.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Does your child understand that 3 + 4 = 5 + 2 can be true even though there is no single “answer after the equals sign”?

capabilities.name: Unknowns & Relational Expressions
capabilities.formal_definition: Reasons about unspecified quantities and relationships represented by blanks, symbols, or simple equations.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover equality alone or pattern growth without an unknown quantity.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If □ + 3 = 8, can your child treat the box as an unknown amount to determine rather than as a signal to start calculating from left to right?

capabilities.name: Shape Properties & Classification
capabilities.formal_definition: Classifies and reasons about 2D and 3D shapes using defining geometric properties rather than superficial appearance.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover general data classification or composing shapes from parts.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If a square is turned like a diamond, does your child still recognize it as a square and explain which properties stayed the same?

capabilities.name: Shape Composition & Decomposition
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands complex shapes as made from simpler geometric parts and simpler shapes as combinable into new shapes.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover number part–whole structure or mental rotation as the main construct.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Can your child combine simple shapes to make a target shape, or identify which smaller shapes make up a larger one?

capabilities.name: Spatial Relations & Orientation
capabilities.formal_definition: Represents and reasons about locations, directions, and relationships among objects or between self and environment.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover transforming an object’s orientation or shape properties.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Can your child follow or describe a route using spatial relationships such as left/right, above/below, or between?

capabilities.name: Spatial Transformation & Visualization
capabilities.formal_definition: Mentally or physically transforms spatial objects and anticipates their resulting orientation or configuration.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover static location/orientation vocabulary or shape classification by properties.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Can your child usually predict how a familiar shape will look after it is turned or flipped, without needing to physically move it first?

capabilities.name: Length Reasoning
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands one-dimensional extent and how length can be compared and measured using iterated units.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover area/coverage, mass, or visual “overall size.”
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: When comparing two objects, does your child know to align the ends rather than judging only by where the far end happens to be?

capabilities.name: Area & Coverage Reasoning
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands two-dimensional coverage and how area can be compared or measured using equal area units.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover length/perimeter, volume, or vague visual size.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If one rectangle is longer but much thinner, can your child avoid assuming it automatically has more area?

capabilities.name: Capacity & Volume Reasoning
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands amount contained and three-dimensional space, including comparison and measurement with equal units.
owned_skill_families: distinguishing container shape from amount held
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover area/coverage or mass/heaviness.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If two differently shaped containers hold the same amount, can your child understand that one is not automatically “more” just because it is taller?

capabilities.name: Mass Reasoning
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands heaviness as a measurable attribute distinct from visual size or volume.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover capacity/volume or general comparison without the mass attribute.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Does your child understand that a smaller-looking object can still be heavier than a larger-looking one?

capabilities.name: Time & Duration Reasoning
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands temporal order, duration, and measurement of elapsed or calendar time.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover number sequence/order unless it is specifically used to represent time.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Can your child compare how long two familiar activities take rather than only knowing which one happens first?

capabilities.name: Angle & Turn Reasoning
capabilities.formal_definition: Understands angle as an amount of turn or opening and compares/measures that attribute independently of line length.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover length of rays/segments or general spatial rotation without angle magnitude.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If two angles have arms of different lengths, can your child focus on how open the angles are rather than which arms look longer?

capabilities.name: Classification & Categorical Organization
capabilities.formal_definition: Organizes objects or cases into categories using explicit attributes and can reorganize them under different valid rules.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover geometric shape classification specifically or graphical representation of collected data.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Can your child sort the same objects in more than one sensible way, such as first by color and then by type?

capabilities.name: Data Representation
capabilities.formal_definition: Converts categorized observations or measurements into organized external representations.
owned_skill_families: mapping observations to marks or symbols
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover interpreting conclusions from a graph as the primary capability.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Can your child turn a small collection of observations into a simple table, tally, or picture graph that preserves the counts?

capabilities.name: Data Interpretation & Comparison
capabilities.formal_definition: Extracts, compares, and reasons from information represented in tables, charts, and simple data displays.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover constructing the representation itself or probability/uncertainty.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Given a simple chart, can your child answer questions such as which category has more and how many more?

capabilities.name: Chance & Probability Reasoning
capabilities.formal_definition: Reasons about uncertainty and relative likelihood of possible outcomes.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover deterministic pattern prediction or interpreting ordinary frequency charts.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Can your child explain why drawing a red block is more likely when a bag contains many red blocks and only one blue block?

capabilities.name: Problem Representation & Modeling
capabilities.formal_definition: Transforms a mathematical situation into a useful representation and interprets mathematical representations back in context.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not own the specific arithmetic/geometry content being represented; it is cross-domain representation competence.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: When facing a new word problem, does your child often make a useful drawing, object model, number sentence, or other representation rather than guessing from keywords?

capabilities.name: Strategy Planning & Mathematical Adaptation
capabilities.formal_definition: Chooses, sequences, and modifies mathematical approaches based on the structure of a problem.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover awareness of one’s own learning state; that belongs to metacognition.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: When the first mathematical approach is awkward, can your child often choose a different mathematical method that fits the problem better?

capabilities.name: Structural Noticing & Generalization
capabilities.formal_definition: Identifies invariant mathematical relationships across examples and formulates a broader structure or rule.
owned_skill_families: creating another instance of the same structure
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover repeating/growing patterns as content unless the key issue is cross-example structural abstraction.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: After seeing several differently presented problems with the same underlying idea, can your child notice and describe what is mathematically the same?

capabilities.name: Mathematical Justification & Critique
capabilities.formal_definition: Evaluates whether a mathematical claim or reasoning is valid and supports judgments with mathematical reasons or counterexamples.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not require polished communication skill; the target is mathematical validity and justification.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: If a character says “2 + 3 = 4,” can your child decide whether it is right and give a mathematical reason or correction?

capabilities.name: Transfer & Analogy
capabilities.formal_definition: Recognizes a previously learned mathematical relationship in a new representation, context, or surface form and applies it appropriately.
owned_skill_families: applying known structure in a novel context
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not mean merely repeating the same skill with different numbers; the context or representation must meaningfully change.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: Can your child use an idea learned with objects in a different setting, such as recognizing the same part–whole relation in a story or equation?

capabilities.name: Understanding & Uncertainty Monitoring
capabilities.formal_definition: Notices and differentiates knowing, uncertainty, confusion, and guessing during mathematical activity.
owned_skill_families: noticing mismatch between result and expectation
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover mathematical plausibility itself; that is MT-04. This capability concerns awareness of one’s own certainty.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: When unsure about a math answer, does your child usually recognize that uncertainty rather than confidently treating a guess as known?

capabilities.name: Strategy Awareness & Progress Monitoring
capabilities.formal_definition: Notices what strategy is being used and whether progress toward a mathematical solution is working.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover selecting the mathematically best strategy itself; selection quality is MT-02, awareness of one’s use is metacognitive.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: After solving a problem, can your child usually tell you what they tried or how they got the answer, even in simple words?

capabilities.name: Learning Regulation & Strategy Switching
capabilities.formal_definition: Takes an appropriate learning action when current understanding or approach is insufficient.
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not cover the mathematical merits of the replacement strategy itself; it concerns regulation in response to monitoring.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: When your child realizes a method is not working, do they often try a different approach, ask for a useful hint, or check their work instead of only repeating the same step?

capabilities.name: Reflection, Review & Consolidation
capabilities.formal_definition: Reconstructs a recent learning experience, identifies the important idea or strategy, and organizes what changed in understanding.
owned_skill_families: identifying what to remember next time
capabilities.boundary_exclusion: Does not score general speaking/communication quality; verbal, visual, or action-based reflection can all count.
capabilities.sample_parent_indicator: After a math activity, can your child usually tell or show you one important thing they learned or a strategy that helped?
